source.title: Safe-SAIL: Towards a Fine-grained Safety Landscape of Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoder Interpretation Framework
source.authors: Jia-Qi Weng; Han Zheng; Hanyu Zhang; Ej Zhou; Qinqin He; Jia-Ling Tao; Hui Xue; Zhixuan Chu; Xi-Ting Wang

page_placements.theme: Measured interpretability depends on the labelling tool, metric, threshold, concept vocabulary, probing data and explainer

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present and readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates how well automated explanations predict feature activations using simulation scores, a different application and set of models from the claim's original neuron-pole audit.
record.gate_note: The study tests automated explanation scoring for SAE features, relevant to V7. It does not audit the share of neuron poles with one or two jobs, compare dense and mixture-of-experts models at scale, test InceptionV1 examples, or build attribution graphs. Results about segment-level simulation efficiency are not results about how many features receive good explanation scores. The steering results deliberately induce behavior and do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study scores explanations of SAE latents (a trained dictionary basis), not the model's own neurons, using simulation correlation as a tool inside its Safe-SAIL framework. The scored latents were also pre-selected as safety-concept-sensitive (precision >0.75, recall >0.2). Its 'interpretable' cut-off is a correlation of 0.2, far below what V7's 'good score' implies. None of V1–V7 is measured on the unit or population the versions name, so the results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' main conclusion is that Safe-SAIL selects SAEs suited to safety-domain interpretability and halves explanation cost via segment-level simulation (r≈0.8 with token-level). Explainer choice matters, and DeepSeek-R1 scored best. They acknowledge explanation quality depends on the explainer and that causal validation is only preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: The study interprets safety-domain SAE features in Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and scores explanations by simulated activation correlation; it does not reproduce the original Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit.
record.method_sensitivity: Explainer model changes the average CorrScore and the share of feature explanations above 0.2. The study also varies SAE location and TopK sparsity in Table 1.

fits_no_version.finding: For safety-filtered SAE latents of Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, the share of explanations with simulation correlation >0.2 depends strongly on the explainer: QwQ-32B 43.11%, DeepSeek-R1 80.46%, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 71.93%. Mean correlations are 0.19–0.33.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automated simulation scores for SAE-feature explanations, at a lenient 0.2 threshold, depend heavily on the explainer model.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean CorrScore of safety SAE latents varies with SAE sparsity and location (0.29–0.38). An LLM-rated superposition score is reported to fall as CorrScore rises.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE configuration choices change how simulatable feature explanations are.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The explanation scores are automated simulations, and the text does not establish that simulation examples were held out from the examples used to write explanations. The 0.2 interpretability threshold is empirically chosen. The primary model is Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct; these results do not assess the broader model and architecture range in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted under the row cap. Segment-level versus token-level simulation comparisons report simulation-method agreement and cost, rather than the proportion of explanations scoring well. Appendix G steering results deliberately induce behavior and do not test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No cross-model or cross-scale neuron shares; no dense versus MoE comparison.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
No comparison of neuron interpretability across architectures or tools.
No neuron-based attribution graphs or replacement-model comparison.
No comparison of fit on activating examples against prediction on held-out text.
No simulation scoring of actual model neurons. Only SAE latents pre-filtered for safety concepts, at a low 0.2 threshold.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V7 labels are dropped for three reasons. First, the scored units are SAE latents rather than neurons, even though the paper calls them 'neurons'. Second, they are selected for concept sensitivity before scoring. Third, 0.2 is a lenient cut-off, unlike the high scores V7 counts as good. Appendix G steering deliberately induces behaviour and is correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or proportions of poles with one job, two jobs, or unknown jobs.
No comparison of similar shares across models, dense versus mixture-of-experts architectures, or models up to trillions of parameters.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron analysis or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No comparison of architecture, regularization, tools, or interpretable-neuron shares in InceptionV1-sized vision models.
No attribution graphs or comparison of neuron-based explanations with a trained replacement model and its reconstruction error.
The study reports simulation scores, but does not establish that explanations were tested on activations withheld from the examples used to write them, or compare performance on those two sets.

The reported threshold is correlation score greater than 0.2 for safety-related SAE feature explanations; the study does not test other thresholds or the broader neuron populations named in the claim.

relation.reason: It uses explanation-and-simulation scoring as a tool on SAE latents and makes no neuron-level test of the claim.

tranche.reason: It scores explanations of SAE latents (a trained dictionary, not model neurons) by simulation correlation, as a tool to choose the explainer inside Safe-SAIL. The latents were pre-filtered for safety concepts (precision >0.75, recall >0.2), so it does not test V7 or any other neuron-level version.

source_check.notes: Table 2 pools features from quartile layers 0/8/17/26/35. Its settings do not name the simulator or restate the safety filtering; the 1058 layer-17 features, simulated by QwQ-32B, come from the separate Sec 3.3 comparison. The paper often calls SAE latents 'neurons' (Appendix B, Table 1 text), and 0.2 is the authors' own human-interpretability cutoff.

statements.correction: Table 2, features pooled from quartile layers 0/8/17/26/35: share with CorrScore >0.2 is QwQ-32B 43.11%, DeepSeek-R1 80.46%, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 71.93%; averages 0.1855, 0.3251, 0.2857.
statements.problem: None. The shares (43.11%, 80.46%, 71.93%) and the averages (0.1855, 0.3251, 0.2857, rounded to 0.19-0.33) match Table 2 for the named explainers. The statement correctly identifies SAE latents of Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and gives no layer or feature count.
